title: --enable-deterministic-inference accepted and reported enabled, but has no effect on an NVFP4 W4A4 + hybrid-Mamba checkpoint with a DFlash2 drafter (GB10 / sm_121)
body:
## Summary

On a GB10 (sm_121, aarch64), `--enable-deterministic-inference` **works
correctly on a dense BF16 model** in the same container image, on the same GPU:
identical concurrent requests collapse from 8 distinct completions to 1.

On a **Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (W4A4) checkpoint with hybrid Mamba layers and a DFlash2
drafter**, the same flag is accepted, appears as
`enable_deterministic_inference=True` in the resolved `ServerArgs`, and
**temperature-0 outputs remain non-reproducible**.

The flag therefore appears not to cover one or more of those paths, and it fails
**silently** — the server reports the feature as on. A user reading the resolved
args has no way to know the guarantee does not apply to their model.

## Why this is worth a report even though the flag "works"

The failure mode is not "deterministic mode is broken". It is **a coverage gap
that presents identically to success**. That is worse than an error, because the
natural check — confirm the flag was applied — passes.

We spent a substantial amount of time excluding four other explanations before
testing the flag against a model simple enough to isolate the hardware. Anyone
running a quantized or hybrid model on this hardware will hit the same wall, and
the resolved-args check will reassure them at exactly the wrong moment.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA GB10, sm_121, aarch64 |
| SGLang | `0.0.0.dev1+g5f55db35e` (locally built dev image, commit `5f55db35e`) |
| torch / CUDA | `2.13.0+cu130` / CUDA 13.0 |
| Attention backend | `flashinfer` |
| Working model | Qwen3-0.6B, **dense BF16** |
| Failing model | Qwen3.8-27B **NVFP4 (W4A4)**, hybrid Mamba layers, DFlash2 drafter |

## Reproducer

The probe fires N identical requests concurrently and counts **distinct
completions**. A batch-invariant server returns exactly one.

```python
# batch_invariance_probe.py <base_url> <model> <n>
import collections, concurrent.futures, hashlib, sys, httpx

BASE, MODEL, N = sys.argv[1].rstrip("/"), sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
PROMPT = ("A backup job writes 47 GB on Monday, then 12% more each day for the "
          "next four days. Compute the total written across all five days, "
          "showing each day's figure to two decimal places.")

def one(_):
    r = httpx.post(f"{BASE}/chat/completions", timeout=900, json={
        "model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}],
        "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0.0})
    r.raise_for_status()
    m = r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]
    text = (m.get("reasoning_content") or "") + "\x00" + (m.get("content") or "")
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N) as ex:
    counts = collections.Counter(ex.map(one, range(N)))
print(f"{N} requests -> {len(counts)} distinct")
```

### Control — dense BF16, flag off then on

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --served-model-name small --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --context-length 8192 --max-running-requests 64 --port 8898
```

```
32 requests -> 8 distinct
```

Adding `--enable-deterministic-inference` to the identical command:

```
32 requests -> 1 distinct
```

**The flag works on this hardware.** sm_121 is not the obstacle.

### Failing case — NVFP4 + Mamba + DFlash2

With `--enable-deterministic-inference` present and confirmed in the resolved
`ServerArgs`, temperature-0 outputs on the 27B NVFP4 checkpoint continue to vary
between identical runs.

### The failing model IS clean at batch 1, which points squarely at batch composition

Measured on the 27B NVFP4 model, **without** the flag, varying only how many of
the 32 identical requests were in flight at once:

| in flight | achieved concurrency | distinct completions from 32 identical temp-0 requests |
|---|---|---|
| 32 | 16 (server-capped) | **20** |
| 1 | 1, verified for every minute of the run | **1 — byte-identical** |

Thirty-two consecutive single-stream requests over seven minutes produced one
distinct answer. So on this checkpoint the nondeterminism is **entirely
batch-composition driven** — exactly what deterministic mode exists to remove,
and exactly what it is not removing here.

(The two rows are not a controlled A/B of batch size: the server caps achieved
concurrency, and the batch-1 run additionally required the server to be otherwise
idle. An earlier batch-1 run with unrelated traffic present returned 3 distinct.
We report that rather than omit it, but we cannot attribute those 3 — that run
lacked per-request timestamps.)

## Two notes that may save a reviewer time

**1. Validate the probe before trusting a clean result from it.** Run the
control arm *first*, flag off. If it returns 1 distinct, the probe cannot detect
nondeterminism on that model and a clean result with the flag means nothing. A
check that cannot fail proves nothing.

**2. Do not use scored benchmark items as the instrument.** We started there and
it was the wrong tool. A weak model gets every hard item wrong every time, which
scores zero flips and looks perfectly deterministic — **uniform failure is
indistinguishable from reproducibility**. Counting distinct completions is both
strictly more sensitive (one flipped token is enough) and orders of magnitude
cheaper.

## What we have not established

We have **not** isolated which of the three features is responsible. NVFP4 W4A4
kernels, the hybrid Mamba layers, and the DFlash2 acceptance path are all
plausible and all present at once in the failing configuration. Separating them
needs three bench servers we have not built. If a maintainer can say which of
those paths deterministic mode is known not to cover, that likely answers it
without the experiment.

We also have not run the concurrent-request probe against the 27B *with the flag
on* — the flag-on evidence for that model is from scored-item flips, which is
the weaker instrument described above. That run requires standing up a second
copy of the 27B, which we have queued.
